spec.assertion: Proves trigger = fullBurstEnter (applies land on fullBurstStart frames, disjoint from aria's burstCast frames) and target = all allies (one apply per comp member per activation). Fails under the nearest-wrong burstCast keying (activation frames differ) and under self-only targeting (teammate totals drop).

Proves stat = generic critDamagePct at exactly 26.99 with a 600-frame (10s) wall-clock window and no durationShots. Fails under a crit-RATE mis-encoding (no other stat may carry 26.99) and under a round-count duration reading.

Proves trigger = lastBullet (per-magazine): activation count equals aria's reload count ±1 and is <30 over 180s on a 300-round belt. Fails under the nearest-wrong shotFired keying (patched counterfactual yields >3x the activations) and under interval keying (cadence would decouple from reloads). Target-set asserted as all allies.

Proves stat = unscoped critRatePct (critRateNormalPct is asserted absent — the scope trap) at 7.03 with a 300-frame window. Non-vacuity: the 5s windows are asserted NOT to blanket the fight, so the intermittency is real rather than an always-on approximation.

Proves a shield effect with maxHpPct=37.86, durationSec=10, target = all allies, emitted once per aria burst cast. Per the tandem/cross-unit rule it is NOT skipped on isolation (it fires teammates' `shielded` triggers). Fails under self-only targeting (counterfactual restricts the target set to aria) and under a targetMaxHpPct reading (magnitude is caster-scaled by the literal text "the skill user's final Max HP").

Proves target = SELF ONLY (the target-set trap: the preceding burst line is allies, this one is not) and duration = 900 frames (15s), distinct from the shield's 10s so the two burst lines cannot be collapsed. Removing it moves aria's total and leaves every teammate byte-identical — fails under an allies-scoped mis-encoding.

it.skip — ALWAYS-⛑ field #7. The kit states the +30.37% Hit Rate, not the resulting core-rate lift; asserting a specific damage delta would encode the engine's hrCoreMult estimate as kit truth. Only the buff's application/value/target/duration are asserted.

Proves aria invents nothing: no damage rider (no dot/flat buckets from her srcSlot), no boss debuff (damageTakenPct absent), no weapon-state modifier (ammo/reload/fire-rate/attack-speed/charge-speed all absent), no ATK grant. Fails if any block adds an unstated mechanic to hit a number.

fixtures: controlComp('aria', true) — the single fixture, one deterministic 180s run plus five counterfactual runs (6 total, well under the ~20-run budget). aria is Burst II, so the control comp's B1 and B3 slots are structurally REQUIRED: without a full I→II→III chain aria never casts and both burst lines plus skill1's full-burst trigger would be untestable. The fixed-B3 flag is left ON for the same reason (a chain needs a B3); it does not confound aria's readings because every discriminating assertion filters buffApply/shield events by casterIdx === aria's slot, and the totals-based counterfactuals compare aria-patched vs aria-unpatched with all other slots held identical. Non-vacuity is asserted explicitly up front: ≥1 fullBurstStart (S1 trigger exercised), ≥1 aria reload (S2 last-bullet trigger exercised), ≥1 aria burstCast (burst slot exercised) — without these the trigger-identity assertions would pass vacuously.
gaps: ⛑ Hit Rate → core-hit magnitude (burst self line): it.skip — measured-only per ALWAYS-⛑ #7; the kit supplies the Hit Rate percentage, not the core-rate lift it produces, so no damage-delta magnitude is asserted.

⛑ MG cadence tuple (pulls/s, wind-up ladder, 161-frame reloadFrames): it.skip — datamine-unreliable per ALWAYS-⛑ #1. It sets the last-bullet cadence, so the S2 activation count is asserted RELATIVE to the observed reload count (±1) and by order-of-magnitude, never against an absolute expected number.

Shield HP amount unobservable: v1 models no HP pool (the boss deals no damage), so the 37.86% value cannot be validated as mitigation. Only emission, caster-scaling flag, target set and 10s duration are testable — recorded as a GAP, not a FIX.
